title: Decouple IO dispatcher and lease reclaimer to reduce tail latency and simplify upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: The current serving runtime couples IO dispatch (network + GPU enqueue) tightly with KV lease reclamation and token allocator logic inside the slot scheduler. This coupling increases tail latency under bursty traffic and makes incremental upgrades risky. The objective is to split the responsibilities: a lightweight IO dispatcher focused on minimal per-request fast-path, and a separately scheduled asynchronous lease reclaimer/allocator that manages KV eviction and slot lifecycle off the hot path.

Scope:
- Extract the IO dispatching codepath into a minimal, no-block fast-path that only performs routing, prefix cache lookup, and GPU enqueue.
- Implement an async lease reclaimer service responsible for: lease expiration, delayed KV eviction, reclaiming stale slots, and emitting metrics.
- Introduce an explicit token allocator micro-protocol used by dispatcher to request temporary KV reservations without waiting for reclaimer work to complete.
- Add clear handoff semantics and backpressure signals between dispatcher and reclaimer.
- Update observability (per-request tracing, per-lease metrics, reclamation latency histograms).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change kernel selection or model compilation logic.
- It does not implement new batching algorithms; we maintain current continuous-batching behavior but reduce IO path contention.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Why now: Recent incidents showed 95th->99th percentile token latency regressions during sudden traffic spikes due to synchronous eviction/lease work. This refactor isolates that work, reducing blast radius and enabling staged rollouts for further scheduler improvements.
acceptance_criteria: P95 end-to-end token latency reduced by >= 15% on synthetic burst tests compared to baseline (same cluster, same load)
Reclamation and eviction are executed asynchronously; dispatcher codepath has no waiting syscall related to lease reclamation in flamegraphs
All existing integration tests (batching, warmup, slot lifecycle) pass under nightly cluster run
New metrics (lease_reclaim_latency_ms, dispatcher_queue_wait_ms, kv_temp_reservations) are emitted and wired to dashboards
Can perform canary rollback with no data corruption and no orphaned KV reservations
implementation_steps: Design handoff protocol and draft API for token allocator (internal RPC over in-process queue)
Create IO dispatcher module and migrate minimal routing/lookup/enqueue logic into it
Implement async lease reclaimer as a pluggable worker with backoff and priority lanes
Add temporary reservation mechanism for short-lived requests and integrate into dispatcher fast-path
Introduce feature flag to toggle async reclaimer behavior per-cluster for canary rollout
Add unit + integration tests; create perf harness for bursty traffic scenarios
Deploy to canary (one dedicated pool) and run load tests and chaos injection
Iterate on metrics and dashboards; wider rollout once P95 target validated
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Race conditions between reservation expiry and reclaimer eviction -> Mitigation: conservative default TTL and strong invariants checked in tests
Risk: Increased memory footprint due to delayed eviction -> Mitigation: circuit breaker in reclaimer and quota-aware reclamation
Risk: Obscure scheduling regressions during upgrade -> Mitigation: feature flag, canary fleet, rollback playbook
Risk: Metrics blind spots -> Mitigation: add explicit tracers and end-to-end synthetic checks
